items.title: Timing of Artificial Intelligence vs Human Identification of Cardiac Amyloidosis on Echocardiography.
The CAST technique: A novel capture-assisted Safari tracking maneuver for radial pigtail repositioning after TAVI.
items.abstract: Right radial access is increasingly used as the sole secondary arterial access during minimalist transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). However, unfavorable right subclavian-aortic arch angulation or marked supra-aortic tortuosity may prevent spontaneous advancement of a radial pigtail catheter into the descending aorta. We describe the CAST (Capture-Assisted Safari Tracking) technique, a simple and reproducible maneuver for repositioning a radial pigtail catheter into the descending aorta using the Safari XS guidewire already in place during TAVI. The technique consists of four sequential steps: encounter, capture, pull-down, and release. The Safari XS guidewire acts as a traction rail, allowing the pigtail loop to be captured and guided in a controlled manner toward the descending aorta. This maneuver enables successful repositioning of the pigtail catheter into the descending aorta despite unfavorable supra-aortic anatomy, without requiring additional arterial access or dedicated equipment. The CAST technique is a simple, reproducible, and equipment-free maneuver that can overcome selected difficulties encountered with radial access during minimalist TAVI. It may reduce repeated catheter and guidewire manipulation and avoid the need for additional femoral access.

items.title: Elevated plasma phenylacetylglutamine is independently associated with heart failure: A cross-sectional biomarker study.
items.abstract: Phenylacetylglutamine (PAGln), a microbial metabolite generated from dietary phenylalanine, has emerged as a candidate mediator in cardiovascular disease, but whether it holds diagnostic value for heart failure (HF) is unclear. We designed a cross-sectional case-control study at Xiangya Hospital, enrolling 104 participants (65 stable HF patients and 39 non-HF controls), to address this question. Plasma PAGln was quantified by ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS). Concentrations were significantly higher in the HF group than in controls (median 1.7 vs. 1.2 μM, P = 0.001). After multivariable adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, lifestyle factors, comorbidities, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, every 1-SD increase in log-transformed PAGln raised HF odds by 95% (odds ratio [OR] 1.95, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.07-3.56, P = 0.030). The top tertile carried 4.57-fold greater odds than the bottom tertile (OR 4.57, 95% CI 1.08-19.45, P = 0.040). On receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, PAGln achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.658 (95% CI 0.551-0.764) with 46.2% sensitivity and 84.6% specificity. PAGln tracked positively with LDL-C, total cholesterol, and fasting glucose, and inversely with estimated glomerular filtration rate. Notably, the highest PAGln levels were seen in HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), with a significant difference between non-HF and HFrEF subgroups (P = 0.01). Collectively, our results indicate that elevated plasma PAGln is independently linked to HF and may reflect disease severity, supporting its potential as a complementary metabolic biomarker for HF evaluation.

items.title: CAD PVAT-Derived Exosomes Impair Endothelial Barrier Function Through the miR-183-5p/TPM1 Axis.
items.abstract: Crosstalk between perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) and vascular endothelial cells plays an important role in vascular homeostasis and atherosclerosis. However, the contribution of PVAT-derived exosomes to coronary endothelial barrier dysfunction remains incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated the effects of PVAT-derived exosomes obtained from patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) and non-CAD surgical controls on human coronary artery endothelial cells and explored the underlying molecular mechanism. Compared with exosomes from non-CAD controls, CAD PVAT-derived exosomes increased endothelial permeability, disrupted F-actin organization, reduced junctional protein expression, and decreased nitric oxide production and endothelial nitric oxide synthase phosphorylation. miR-183-5p was enriched in CAD PVAT-derived exosomes, and miR-183-5p overexpression reproduced several features of endothelial dysfunction. Dual-luciferase reporter assays identified tropomyosin 1 (TPM1) as a direct target of miR-183-5p. Importantly, inhibition of miR-183-5p attenuated CAD PVAT-exosome-induced endothelial dysfunction, whereas TPM1 overexpression partially reversed the detrimental effects of miR-183-5p. Together, these findings suggest that the miR-183-5p/TPM1 axis contributes to CAD PVAT-exosomes mediated endothelial barrier dysfunction and may represent a potential link between PVAT dysfunction and atherosclerosis.

Cancer-Associated Fibroblasts and Tertiary Lymphoid Structures: Critical Regulators in the Tumor Immune Microenvironment.
items.abstract: Tumor-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are a highly heterogeneous cell population. Although previous studies have largely associated CAFs with tumor invasion and drug resistance, recent evidence has linked certain CAFs subsets to tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) within the tumor immune microenvironment. TLS are lymphocyte aggregates that form in various solid tumors, and their density and location are closely associated with treatment response and prognosis. However, specific studies on CAFs within the TLS niche remain limited and fragmented, underscoring an urgent need for systematic synthesis. By reviewing recent advances in relevant studies, we innovatively propose a "CAFs-TLS axis" framework. This framework does not claim to uncover new biological mechanisms; rather, it summarizes the distinct CAFs subsets within the TLS niche and elaborates on how CAFs participate in or suppress the entire process of TLS initiation, recruitment, maturation, and re-aggregation. We further discuss how different therapeutic strategies affect the "CAFs-TLS axis." This framework will provide a theoretical basis for developing strategies that target CAFs to induce TLS formation, enhance therapeutic efficacy, and strengthen antitumor immune responses, ultimately improving clinical outcomes for cancer patients.

items.title: Nanoengineering strategies for precision regulation of chimeric antigen receptor T-cell-induced cytokine release syndrome.
items.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy faces a critical clinical hurdle: cytokine release syndrome (CRS). Current CRS management strategies have limited selectivity and may interfere with CAR-T cell antitumor activity, highlighting the need for more targeted and precisely controllable interventions. Nanoengineering offers a promising approach to address these limitations by enabling the spatiotemporally controlled monitoring and modulation of inflammatory responses, with the potential to mitigate excessive cytokine release while preserving CAR-T cell therapeutic efficacy, driving a paradigm shift toward programmable, proactive immune regulation. This review systematically examines nanointervention strategies for mitigating CAR-T-induced CRS, including molecular monitoring, cytokine clearance, targeted delivery, stimulus-responsive systems, biomimetic designs, and genetic reprogramming. These approaches enable precise intervention across multiple stages-from early inflammation detection and localized neutralization to source-level cellular engineering. Finally, we discuss challenges in biosafety, clinical translation, and the potential of artificial intelligence-driven predictive platforms. Nanotechnology offers a transformative pathway to redefine CRS from an unpredictable complication into a manageable therapeutic window, paving the way for safer next-generation cellular immunotherapies.

items.title: Assessment of peripheral and tumor specific Tregs and Th17 cells in patients with endometrial cancer.
items.abstract: The frontline treatment for endometrial cancer (EC) is a hysterectomy; immunotherapy is approved, but has limited efficacy in all EC genotypes (mismatch repair genotypes). Understanding how EC pathogenesis affects the immune response is essential to determine effective interventions. Systemic inflammation, driven by T helper 17 (Th17) cells is induced in many cancers, while tumor induction of suppressive T regulatory cells (Tregs) is critical for immune evasion. We hypothesized that patients with EC have peripheral inflammation (evidenced by increased Th17:Treg ratio); yet, the EC tumor microenvironment (TME) remains immune tolerant (high Treg localization). We collected peripheral blood and endometrial tissue from 61 patients with EC and 15 controls on the day-of-surgery, and blood post-surgical intervention (PSI). Peripheral Tregs and Th17 populations were examined via fluorescence activated cell sorting, plasma cytokine levels were measured utilizing immune assays, and tissue abundance of Th17 and Tregs via immunohistochemistry. Compared to controls, patients with early-stage (I, II) EC exhibited decreased peripheral unconventional Tregs (uTregs) and total Tregs, without changes in Th17 cell populations or the overall peripheral Th17:Treg ratio. Patients with proficient MMR genotyping also had reduced peripheral Treg populations. Patients with advanced disease (III, IV) had elevated peripheral inflammatory cytokines. The TME, regardless of stage, had increased abundance of Foxp3 + , but decreased RORγt + cells. EC patients had reduced peripheral inflammatory cytokine production at PSI. EC patients exhibited increased peripheral inflammation, which decreased after tumor removal. EC TME indicated potential immune evasion through increased Tregs, but decreased Th17 localization within the tumor.

items.title: Macrophage-centered resistance programs in cancer: A unified framework for therapeutic resistance and precision immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Therapeutic resistance remains a major barrier to durable cancer control despite advances in immunotherapy, targeted therapy, cellular therapies, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy. Although tumor cell-intrinsic genetic and epigenetic alterations are well-established drivers of resistance, treatment outcomes are also shaped by dynamic interactions within the tumor microenvironment (TME). Among its stromal and immune constituents, tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are prominent regulators of therapeutic resistance because of their functional plasticity and capacity to integrate diverse environmental signals. Here, we introduce macrophage-centered resistance programs as an integrative framework comprising four recurrent, non-mutually exclusive functional modules: lipid-associated, matrix-remodeling, glyco-immune, and metabolic programs. These modules link tumor-derived stressors to macrophage adaptation, immune suppression, stromal remodeling, and therapeutic persistence, while allowing substantial overlap, context dependence, and dynamic interconversion. We further distinguish associative observations from mechanistic and causal evidence and examine how macrophage-associated resistance mechanisms interact with treatment-specific tumor cell-intrinsic pathways across immune checkpoint blockade, cellular therapy, targeted therapy, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy. Finally, we discuss macrophage-directed therapeutic strategies and the requirements for biomarker-guided precision immunotherapy, including clinical validation, assay standardization, and longitudinal monitoring. This framework is intended as a testable organizational model for understanding macrophage-mediated therapeutic resistance and guiding more precise macrophage-directed interventions.

items.title: Rituximab for immune-mediated diseases with oral mucosal involvement: Mechanisms, evidence, and clinical use.
items.abstract: Persistent oral erosions, pain, xerostomia, and scarring occur in several immune-mediated diseases that involve the oral mucosa. Corticosteroids and conventional immunosuppressants can control activity, but relapse and cumulative toxicity complicate prolonged use. Rituximab (RTX), a chimeric anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody, consistently depletes circulating B cells and has a more variable effect in tissues. Randomized studies provide the clearest support in pemphigus, particularly when RTX is combined early with a short prednisone course. In severe or refractory mucous membrane pemphigoid, including ocular, laryngeal, and other high-risk disease, evidence comes mainly from observational studies and expert recommendations. The evidence is much less certain for oral lichen planus, primary Sjögren disease, chronic erythema multiforme, and other inflammatory conditions with oral findings; routine RTX treatment is not justified in these settings. Before prescribing RTX, clinicians should confirm the diagnosis and consider hepatitis B status, baseline immunoglobulin levels, vaccination status, infection risk, and the need for follow-up monitoring. In this narrative review, the biology of B cell depletion is considered alongside the evidence for individual diseases, treatment choices, safety, and priorities for further study.

items.title: Superiority of magnetic resonance elastography and proton density fat fraction: an umbrella meta-analysis of non-invasive imaging for hepatic steatosis and fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and chronic hepatitis B.
items.abstract: Various quantitative techniques based on ultrasound (US) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) have been widely used to assess hepatic steatosis and fibrosis. This study thus aimed to synthesize and critically evaluate the evidence derived from systematic reviews on the diagnostic performance of noninvasive imaging techniques including transient elastography (TE), point shear wave elastography (pSWE), two-dimensional shear wave elastography (2D-SWE), magnetic resonance elastography (MRE), controlled attenuation parameter (CAP), and proton density fat fraction (PDFF) for liver fibrosis and steatosis in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and chronic hepatitis B (CHB). Searches were performed on PubMed, Embase, the Web of Science, and Cochrane Library from database inception until 2 March 2025, including keywords 'liver diseases', imaging', 'systematic review' and others. We included systematic reviews that comprised studies evaluating the diagnostic performance of non-invasive imaging techniques for liver fibrosis or steatosis in patients with MASLD or CHB. Thirty-five reviews were included from 3,752 articles. For hepatic steatosis assessment, PDFF demonstrated high diagnostic stability, while CAP showed good screening performance for mild steatosis. For liver fibrosis assessment, MRE exhibited high diagnostic accuracy for significant (≥F2), advanced (≥F3) fibrosis, and cirrhosis (F4). In obese MASLD patients, MRE demonstrated superior specificity compared to TE. Among CHB patients, MRE displayed particularly high diagnostic performance. Other techniques (2D-SWE, TE) remained clinically valuable in specific stages and patient populations. MRE performance varied between the two etiologies, suggesting liver stiffness is a composite biomarker. PDFF provides precise quantification of steatosis, while CAP is suitable for screening mild cases. The findings emphasize the necessity of developing personalized imaging strategies based on etiology to optimize patient management and reduce reliance on liver biopsy.

items.title: Characterization of lactylation-related genes for predictive model development and molecular subtyping in HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma.
items.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is the leading risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Lactylation-related genes (LRGs) participate in HCC progression, yet their roles in HBV-associated HCC (HBV-HCC) remain largely unclear. In this study, we screened differentially expressed LRGs (DE-LRGs) from HBV-HCC transcriptomic data using weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and built a high-precision random forest prediction model. Three hub genes (RACGAP1, STMN1, ILF2) were verified to be overexpressed in HBV-HCC tissues across multiple datasets and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), and their high expression correlated with unfavorable overall survival and distinct immune infiltration. A three-gene nomogram was constructed in the GSE47197 cohort, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.928 validated by calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA) and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. External validation in GSE121248 reached an AUC of 0.965, verifying its robust predictive power. Moreover, consensus clustering divided HBV-HCC into two LRG-based molecular subtypes, where Cluster 2 had worse prognosis. Collectively, this study establishes an LRG-based predictive model and identifies two molecular subtypes for HBV-HCC, providing reliable and promising biomarker candidates for HBV-HCC risk prediction and individualized immunotherapy.

items.title: Profound Hyperbilirubinemia During Severe Carbon Monoxide Poisoning and Subsequent Multiorgan Failure: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Carbon monoxide poisoning is classically associated with neurologic and cardiovascular toxicity, while severe exposure may also cause systemic toxic-hypoxic injury. Profound direct-predominant hyperbilirubinemia without mechanical biliary obstruction is rarely described. We report a 55-year-old woman with alcohol use disorder, chronic tobacco use, COPD, and hepatic steatosis who presented with altered mental status and jaundice after suspected household carbon monoxide exposure. Her carboxyhemoglobin level was > 30%, and she required intubation, intensive care, vasopressor support, and three hyperbaric oxygen treatments. Initial testing showed total bilirubin of 23.1 mg/dL and direct bilirubin of 13.1 mg/dL, despite only mild AST elevation and near-normal ALT and alkaline phosphatase. Imaging showed hepatic steatosis and cholelithiasis without convincing biliary obstruction, and the documented workup for viral, autoimmune, metabolic, hemolytic, and vascular causes was unrevealing. Her liver dysfunction was considered multifactorial, with possible carbon monoxide-related toxic-hypoxic injury superimposed on underlying steatotic or alcohol-related liver vulnerability. After transient improvement, she developed coagulopathy, acute kidney injury, recurrent shock with clinical and imaging concern for acute cholecystitis, worsening hyperbilirubinemia peaking near 49-50 mg/dL, encephalopathy, respiratory failure, and multiorgan failure. Cholecystostomy yielded dark green bile without documented purulence, and aspirate cultures showed no growth; biliary sepsis was therefore not microbiologically confirmed. She died in the hospital after goals-of-care discussions. The initial bilirubin-predominant pattern was atypical for classic hypoxic hepatitis and may have reflected overlapping hepatic insults. This case emphasizes broad evaluation and cautious causal interpretation; it does not establish that carbon monoxide exposure alone caused the initial hyperbilirubinemia.

items.title: Simultaneous Contralateral Quadriceps Tendon and Patellar Tendon Rupture in a Patient with Chronic Kidney Disease and HCV Infection: A Rare Case Report.
items.abstract: Extensor mechanism injuries of the knee are uncommon and typically involve either the quadriceps tendon or the patellar tendon. Simultaneous contralateral rupture of the quadriceps tendon on the one side and the patellar tendon on the other is extremely rare. Systemic conditions such as chronic kidney disease (CKD), chronic liver disease, ochronosis, collagen disorders, and hepatitis C virus (HCV) are known to predispose to tendon weakness and rupture even after trivial trauma. A 51-year-old male, a known case of CKD and HCV infection, presented in casualty with inability to walk following trivial trauma. Clinical examination revealed a suprapatellar gap with loss of active extension in the right knee and an infrapatellar gap with loss of active extension in the left knee. Radiographs showed features suggestive of quadriceps tendon rupture (patella baja) on the right side and patellar tendon rupture (patella alta) on the left side. The patient underwent open surgical repair of both tendons using non-absorbable Ethibond sutures with transosseous fixation. Postoperatively, the patient was immobilized, followed by gradual rehabilitation. At follow-up, satisfactory functional recovery with restoration of knee extension was achieved. Simultaneous contralateral quadriceps and patellar tendon rupture is a rare entity, particularly in patients with systemic comorbidities such as CKD and HCV. A high index of suspicion, thorough bilateral knee examination, and early surgical intervention are essential for favorable outcomes.

items.title: Validation of Ontario criteria for patients transplanted with hepatocellular carcinoma.
items.abstract: Liver transplantation (LT) is a curative treatment option for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with different listing criteria available. Data on expected survival of patients with regard to the Ontario criteria (OC), and predictive performance of its components, is warranted. Within the United Network for Organ Sharing registry, patients with HCC, and complete tumor information at the time of listing were included. Survival analysis, prediction performance (area under the receiving operating curve (AUROC)) for post-transplantation overall survival (OS), and multivariable regression was conducted. Differences of OC compared to the Milan Criteria (MC) were investigated. The 29,086 patients with HCC having received LT have a median age of 60years(IQR:55,64), 22,303 (77%) male, and a median Model of End-stage Liver Disease score of 10(IQR:8,14). Patients within OC reached a post-transplant 5-year OS of 76%(95%CI:75,76), median OS 13.5years (95%CI:13.2,13.9), and HCC-associated deaths occurred in 8.0% at 5 years. OC's performance for 10-years OS corresponds to an AUROC of 62%(95%CI:61,63). 'Within-MC-beyond-OC' have a higher mortality hazard rate compared to 'within-MC-within-OC' (aHR:1.83; 95%CI:1.60,2.10) - driven by high alpha fetoprotein (AFP) levels. The OC are associated with excellent results. Incorporating AFP appears to improve risk stratification of HCC patients listed for LT.

items.title: Running title: The plasticity of CAFs in cancer development.
items.abstract: Cancer is among the leading causes of death worldwide. The tumor microenvironment is a dynamic, multifaceted milieu where the cancer cells interact with diverse components. Resident stromal cell-derived cancer-associated fibroblasts are central to the crosstalk. There is variability in the origin, phenotype, and function of CAFs, which is influenced by signaling cues from cancer cells and the extracellular matrix. The presence of CAFs in the TME coincides with tumorigenesis, invasion, metastasis, and drug resistance. Many mechanisms are involved, such as metabolic reprogramming of glucose, amino acid, and lipid metabolism. For example, enhanced lactate production can contribute to a glucose-lactate shuttle that supports tumor growth. Dysregulation of normal ECM remodeling leads to a breakdown of the basement membrane, thereby enabling tumor cells to invade. Besides contributing to poor prognosis, CAFs may induce cancer cells to create vascular-like networks. They also recruit immunosuppressive cells and inhibit the immune response. Consequently, deciphering how the different factors affecting the fate and function of CAFs signal and modulate their activities is imperative in fully grasping the complex biology of cancer to seek more effective therapeutic options. By targeting key pathways, surface markers, and conversion of CAFs to a quiescent state, the therapeutic outcome of the treatments for cancers may be improved. In this review, we summarize current knowledge on the biology of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), highlighting how distinct CAF subtypes defined by markers such as α-SMA, FAP, and MHC II (apCAFs), as well as inflammatory (iCAFs) and myofibroblastic (myCAFs) profiles-modulate extracellular matrix remodeling, metabolism, angiogenesis, immune responses, and metastatic potential. Our detailed review goes beyond explaining the potential of CAFs in developing and progressing cancer and addresses areas of research that could enable the widespread translation of this science for effective cancer therapy. Translational work and well-designed clinical trials will be required to fully transform CAFs from facilitators of resistance to actionable targets.
items.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry

items.title: Unusual Morphologic Variants of Solitary Fibrous Tumor: A Case Series of 17 Cases Featuring 10 Distinct Histomorphologies.
items.abstract: Solitary fibrous tumors (SFTs) are mesenchymal neoplasms characterized by spindled-to-ovoid cells, fibrous stroma, prominent staghorn vasculature and harbor characteristic NAB2::STAT6 fusion. Although most SFTs are readily recognized histologically, some display unusual morphologic features that mimic other mesenchymal neoplasms and obscure the diagnosis. Following institutional review board approval, we identified 17 SFTs with unusual morphologic features from our institutional archives. Clinicopathologic features, immunohistochemistry, molecular findings, and Demicco risk stratification were reviewed. Molecular confirmation was available by RNA-based next-generation sequencing fusion panel. The cohort included 17 tumors (9 males, 8 females). Sites included deep soft tissue of pelvis (n=3), thigh (2), abdominal wall (1), dermis of temple (1), sinonasal tract (2) and visceral sites including liver (n=3), lung (n=2), brain (1), thyroid (1), and stomach (1). Median tumor size was 6 cm (range 3.5-15 cm). Histologic patterns included angiosarcoma-like (n=2), pleomorphic liposarcoma-like (n=2), osteosarcoma-like (n=2) with one showing true heterologous osteosarcomatous differentiation, GLI1-altered neoplasm-like (n=3), conventional small round cell morphology (n=4) including one with Ewing-sarcoma-like immunophenotype, pseudoglandular (n=1), low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma-like (n=1), soft tissue angiofibroma-like (n=1), and sinonasal glomangiopericytoma-like (n=1). Five tumors were considered morphologically consistent with dedifferentiated SFT. All tumors retained at least focal conventional SFT morphology. STAT6 IHC was positive in 16/17 tumors; NAB2::STAT6 fusion was confirmed in all 11 cases tested. SFTs may display a wide range of histologic patterns mimicking other benign and malignant mesenchymal neoplasms. Awareness of these variants and integration of IHC and molecular studies are critical to avoid misdiagnosis.

items.title: Targeting PDGFRβ from radiopharmacy to nuclear medicine: Translational implementation of [ 68 Ga]Ga-ATH001 PET/CT at an academic center.
items.abstract: Positron emission tomography (PET) enables non-invasive whole-body assessment of molecular biomarkers and is particularly valuable for evaluating heterogeneous diseases such as cancer. Platelet-derived growth factor receptor beta (PDGFRβ) is a stromal biomarker expressed on activated pericytes and fibroblasts that contributes to tumour remodelling, vascular regulation and therapeutic resistance. This study describes the translational implementation of the PDGFRβ-targeting PET tracer [ 68 Ga]Ga-ATH001, from GMP-compliant radiopharmaceutical development to its first reported oncology application in patients with liver tumours. A GMP-compliant automated synthesis of [ 68 Ga]Ga-ATH001 was established using a ModularLab PharmTracer synthesizer and validated for clinical use. The tracer was prospectively implemented in the IMAGINE-1 study (EU CT 2025-522290-11-00). PET imaging included dynamic liver acquisition immediately after injection, followed by whole-body PET/CT imaging and delayed liver scans to assess tracer biodistribution, tumour uptake and tracer kinetics. [ 68 Ga]Ga-ATH001 was successfully translated into clinical production using an automated in-house synthesis process, achieving a decay-corrected radiochemical yield of 51.9 ± 0.7 %, radiochemical purity of 97 %, radiochemical stability of 96.3 ± 0.5 % after 2 h at room temperature and apparent molar activity of 47.2 ± 1.6 GBq/µmol at EOS. Three consecutive production runs assessed reproducibility; a fourth batch served as a microbiological worst-case challenge and was excluded from the assessment. PET/CT imaging in three patients with colorectal liver metastases showed SUV peak tumour-to-background ratios of 1.5 to 1.8 at 60 min after injection. GMP-compliant production enabled the first reported oncology application of [ 68 Ga]Ga-ATH001 in patients with liver tumours. The ongoing phase 1 IMAGINE-1 study will further evaluate its clinical potential. Clinical Trials Information system: CTIS, EU CT 2025-522290-11-00, Registered 29 September 2025, IMAGINE-1 | 2025-522290-11-00 | CTIS.eu.

items.title: Use of a c-Met-targeting aptamer-drug conjugate for efficient therapy in both primary and metastatic uveal melanoma.
items.abstract: Uveal melanoma (UM), the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults, is associated with a high risk of metastasis, recurrence, and irreversible vision loss. However, current therapeutic options remain limited by insufficient efficacy and poor vision preservation. Building upon the molecular design of SL1-MMAE, a c-Met-targeting aptamer-drug conjugate (ApDC), here we investigate its potential translational application as a targeted therapeutic strategy for both primary and metastatic UM. SL1-MMAE exhibits high binding specificity, rapid cellular internalization, and potent cytotoxicity toward UM cells in vitro. In vivo, SL1-MMAE effectively suppresses tumor growth in both subcutaneous xenograft and liver metastasis models, significantly prolonging survival. Notably, in an orthotopic intraocular UM model, a single intravitreal injection of SL1-MMAE induces robust tumor regression without detectable ocular toxicity at the therapeutic dose. The small molecular size of the ApDC enables superior tumor penetration and reduced retention from non-target ocular tissues. These features are particularly advantageous within the confined intraocular environment, leading to enhanced therapeutic efficacy with improved safety. Compared with the clinically advanced c-Met antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) ABBV-399, the ApDC demonstrates superior antitumor activity and ocular biocompatibility for intraocular UM therapy. Nevertheless, as a preclinical study, further safety, pharmacokinetic and translational studies are warranted to better define the clinical potential of SL1-MMAE. Collectively, these findings establish c-Met-targeting ApDCs as a promising platform for the treatment of both primary and metastatic UM, offering a vision-preserving therapeutic strategy with potent antitumor efficacy and favorable safety profiles.
